streaming.note: Uncountable. Often before another noun: "a streaming service", "music streaming".

monitor.note: Most often a verb, "to watch and check": "Nurses monitor the patients."

slide.note: Often a verb, "to move smoothly": "The door slides open." In a park, a slide is for kids.

ex: Can you take a selfie with us?
She posted a new selfie online.
He took a selfie at the beach.
No selfies in the museum, please.
I made a booking at the hotel for Friday.
Can I change my booking to next week?
The online booking took only two minutes.
She has a booking for two at eight.
booking.note: In the US, people often say "reservation": "a hotel reservation".

trillion.note: After a number, no "s": "two trillion dollars".

crush.note: Most often a verb, "to press and break": "Crush the garlic." Say "have a crush on someone".

ex: The buses come at ten-minute intervals.
Take this medicine at regular intervals.
We have a short interval between the two classes.
How long is the interval between trains?
interval.note: Often "at regular intervals" (= again and again, with the same time between).

ex: She works as an event coordinator at a hotel.
Please talk to the project coordinator about this.
The volunteer coordinator called me this morning.
Who is the coordinator for this trip?

liberal.note: Most often an adjective: "liberal ideas". In the US, a liberal is a person on the political left.

baggage.note: Uncountable: some baggage, a piece of baggage (not "a baggage"). Also "luggage".

ex: Herr Schmidt is our new German teacher.
"Good morning, Herr Weber," said the students.
Can I speak to Herr Müller, please?
The letter is for Herr Klein in Berlin.
Herr.note: A German title, like "Mr.": "Herr Schmidt". Used for German-speaking men.

ex: A leopard is sleeping on a tree branch.
The leopard has beautiful spotted fur.
We saw a leopard at the zoo today.
Leopards usually hunt alone at night.
The paramedic checked his pulse and breathing.
Paramedics arrived in an ambulance in five minutes.
She works as a paramedic in the city.
The paramedics took him to the hospital.
Our company has an audit every year.
The tax office wants to do an audit.
The audit found several mistakes in the reports.
When will the audit be finished?
My son has asthma and uses an inhaler.
Cold air can make her asthma worse.
He had an asthma attack during the race.
Do you have asthma or any allergies?
Gamma is the third letter of the Greek alphabet.
Gamma rays can pass through thick walls.
Doctors use gamma rays to treat some cancers.
In math class, we use gamma as a symbol.
gamma.note: Most often in "gamma rays", a strong kind of radiation.

ex: I got an SMS with a code from my bank.
Can you send me an SMS when you arrive?
The app sends you an SMS reminder before your visit.
Most people now use chat apps instead of SMS.
SMS.note: Americans usually say "text" or "text message": "Text me when you arrive."

ex: Pioneers moved west to the frontier.
Life on the frontier was very hard.
Many families built farms on the frontier.
The old western movie shows life on the frontier.
frontier.note: Also a border, or the edge of what we know: "the frontiers of medicine".

ex: A troll left rude comments under my post.
Please don't answer him, he's just a troll.
The website blocked several trolls this week.
In the old story, a troll lives under a bridge.
troll.note: Also a verb: "to troll" = to post rude things online to make people angry.

consensus.note: Common phrase: "reach a consensus" (= everyone agrees).

maniac.note: Often informal: "He drives like a maniac" (= very fast and dangerously).

upgrade.note: Also a verb: "upgrade your phone" (= get a better or newer one).

boulevard.note: In street names often written "Blvd.": "Ocean Blvd."

ex: My son takes karate lessons after school.
She has a black belt in karate.
Karate teaches children focus and discipline.
Do you want to try a karate class?
Please don't speak to me in that tone.
Her tone was friendly and calm.
I didn't like the tone of his email.
This makeup matches my skin tone.
tone.note: Common: "tone of voice", "in an angry tone". Also a sound: "Leave a message after the tone."

ex: Enzymes help the body digest food.
This enzyme helps break down sugar.
The washing powder has special enzymes.
Some people lack the enzyme to digest milk.
The cheerleaders danced during the football game.
My sister is a cheerleader at her school.
The cheerleaders practice every afternoon after class.
Do you want to be a cheerleader?

freeway.note: American English. Also "highway"; in British English, "motorway".

ex: My game controller stopped working this morning.
Can I borrow your controller for this game?
You need two controllers to play together.
The new controller has better buttons.
controller.note: Also a job: an "air traffic controller" guides planes.

ex: The dictator ruled the country for thirty years.
People finally stood up against the dictator.
The dictator controlled all the newspapers and TV.
My boss acts like a dictator at work.

ole.note: Usually written "olé". "Ole" alone often means "old" in informal speech: "the good ole days".

cashmere.note: Uncountable: "made of cashmere", "a cashmere sweater" (not "a cashmere").

ex: My grandpa loves watching old westerns on TV.
Every western has cowboys, horses, and guns.
Do you want to watch a western tonight?
This old western was filmed in the desert.
western.note: Most often an adjective, "in the west": "western Ukraine", "Western Europe".

ex: The pilot jumped out of the plane with a parachute.
Her parachute opened right on time.
The soldiers landed safely by parachute.
Always check your parachute before you jump.

boiler.note: In the US, a hot water tank is often called a "water heater".

ex: Our school has a new science curriculum this year.
Is swimming part of the school curriculum?
The teachers are changing the math curriculum.
English is in the curriculum from the first grade.
curriculum.note: Plural: "curricula" or "curriculums". It means all the subjects taught at a school.

ex: Tickets for the gala concert sold out quickly.
The orchestra gave a gala concert for charity.
Are you going to the gala concert on Saturday?
Famous singers performed at the gala concert.
gala concert.note: English speakers often just say "a gala" or "a gala evening".

ex: Cannabis is legal in some countries now.
Some doctors prescribe medical cannabis for pain.
He was caught growing cannabis at home.
Smoking cannabis can affect your memory.
The liver removes toxins from the body.
Some wild mushrooms contain deadly toxins.
The factory released toxins into the river.
Snake venom is a very strong toxin.
People had big parties for the new millennium.
The city is more than a millennium old.
Where were you at the start of the millennium?
This church was built almost a millennium ago.
millennium.note: Plural: "millennia". It means 1,000 years; "the new millennium" = the time after 2000.

ex: Add a teaspoon of vanilla extract to the cake.
This face cream contains natural plant extracts.
Green tea extract is used in many drinks.
Can I use lemon extract instead of lemon juice?
extract.note: Most often a verb, "to take out": "extract a tooth". Stress: verb ex-TRACT, noun EX-tract.

print.note: Most often a verb: "print a document" (= put it on paper with a printer).
